Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
!Brujah have good vampires, a oust discipline (presence). They are playable and have many options (bruise&bleed, fight, vote)
!Nosferatu have good support vampires (weenie obf), some stars (Beast) and some interesting strategies (Vermin Channel, and some have dominate). Not terrific but not the worst.
!Gangrel have very little for themselves. Some support vampires (weenie obf again), non ousting disciplines. Some vampires are pretty good though (Sebastian Goulet), some allies are great (Shadow Court Satyr) and Leathery Hide led to some new archetype (www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2k7badia2dec or www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2011rautakanki)

Still, I'd say that the !Gangrel deserve the boost.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Louhi
Messages.Body:
!Gangrel suffer from bad synergy between disciplines, aggravated damage and celerity don't really match, obfuscate is a delivery discipline but the other disciplines hardly offer any actions worth delivering. I do believe it is possible to work around though, to an extent.

The main issue, however, is their crypt. It's split in two and even have a lot of weird disciplines splashed in. They do have one of the biggest weenie crypts available (with a superior soak not requiring any discipline) as well as some really infamous star vampires (Aksynya, Una, Enkidu). You hardly ever play them as a 'clan' efficiently though.

Personally I like them having a bit of a vote angle (city gangrel connections for example) since I believe it's one of the few ways to make their disciplines worth the time. They lack somewhat in build in votes for this though.

Lidingö Scourge

While synergistic, from the standpoint of winning, Celerity and Potence are redundant. Presence has no synergy with either outside of multidiscipline cards.

The most important elements in the game are (largely) missing - intercept, stealth, bleed bounce. Compare with Toreador/!, who get intercept and bounce. There's a reason Brujah (and everybody else who can) play with Dominate all of the time, foregoing Presence, which is the best discipline of the three in isolation. Even then, Brujah have the benefit of Traditions and they still have historically sucked in comparison to other Cammie clans, only achieving a much higher rate of wins in recent years.

Pot/Pre/Obf - vastly better. Cel/Pre/Obf - vastly better. Could even argue for something like Cel/Pot/Ani would be more useful. I'd rather have the Osebo discipline mix than the Brujah/! mix. Vote may be hard to find in the game outside of Presence, but bleed is easy to find.

Messages.Author: Drain
Messages.Body:
!Gangrel took my preference. They really do need some sort of cohesion enhancement for non-superstar all-in-clan crypts to be playable. This ought to mean some clan card of sorts or dual discipline that they all share, as was pointed out. I suggest it not being a combat card because these tend to be less swingy overall.

One other way would be to augment their cohesion by bridging their discipline differentials, similar to what Lord Ashton did for the Gangrel. A couple of cards like these could turn their disparate crypts into something more pointed.

> Predatory Adaptability
>
> Unique Master - Gangrel Antitribu
>
> Put this card in play. You may tap this card to move a blood and a [cel], [ani], [for] or [obf] discipline card from your ash-heap to a ready Gangrel Antitribu you control. You may tap this card to give you an additional discard phase action.
>
Not overly powerful, instead aiming for versatile.

> Pack Bonding
> Gangrel Antitribu
> +1 Stealth Action
>
> Choose a ready Gangrel Antitribu younger than the acting vampire. That vampire gains a blood and a level from one of the acting vampire's superior disciplines. If this action is sucessful, the acting vampire untaps.
>
Similar to Sanguine Instruction but with some obvious perks. I like how this works thematically well with Bay and Owl.

Drain

Messages.Author: bakija
Messages.Body:
> Haze wrote:
> yes that's right. !Gangrel are weaker than Assamites.
>
While I totally agree with you, I have been recently playing a not horrible !Gangrel deck--all the guys in G3/4 who are 4 cap and smaller, and then 2 each of Hartmut and Mugur (both Arch Bishops). Basically a very master heavy (40%; multiple Parthenons) breed/boon bloat political deck that uses a lot of Bay and Howl to get the big guys out fast. Hardly super optimal, using Protean and Obfuscate for stealth and combat defense, but not horrible. Granted, the only thing the !Gangrel angle has going for it is the Bays and Howls (10% of the deck), but certainly playable and wins occasionally.

As noted by, well, everyone already, the !Gangrel lack discipline cohesion and ousting power. Leathery Hide isn't horrible. Bay and Howl is strongish. City Gangrel Connections gives them a little help in the voting department (although, for the love of puck rock, why Una doesn't have Obfustcate is beyond me. Oh, wait. Then she'd be even more insanely broken. Make her "Once per turn, Una may pay 1 less blood for a fortitude card" and turn the dem into OBF...). Giving them a clan specific card that gives them some bleed potential (and doesn't blow) and they might have a fighting chance.

To address Jeff's question:

A) Una: A broken one trick pony. It's a really good trick, but that's all she does. And results in one of those decks that either gets shut down instantly due to a Pentex, a DI, or a preemptive insanely effective rush *or* she goes off and either just wins or ruins the game for everyone but her.

B ) Enkidu: Not really a one trick pony, but in my experience (which, re: Enkidu, is pretty vast) tends to make decks that don't win but do ruin the game for anyone sitting next to him, either by being a huge silly, crater making combat deck that has a lot of trouble actually winning *or* by being some Raptor "Really! I can deck you and win with a Brinksmanship!" abomination. I have seen decks with Enkidu win games (very) seldomly. I have seen decks with Enkidu just make a game a huge mess, ruin people, and directly contribute to someone else winning (very) often.

C) Aksinya: A very good support vampire. Who costs 9. She isn't winning any games on her own. But she has an almost unique mechanic attached to her (use master cards for something other than being master cards or discards; Pariah is the only other minion who does something like this IIRC, and his ability is vastly worse, although still something to build a deck around once and a while for fun), so she will show up in decks that want to really maximize master use and needs bleed bounce grafted in. Like when hanging out with Cybele. But Aksinya is rarely going to be the main focus of the deck--she is going to be the adjunct that provides bounce support and master cycling.

Yeah, on checking, about a third (13 or so) of the !Gangrel decks in the TWDA are crypts that are mostly and broadly !Gangrel (i.e. the crypt is, like, 8+ !Gangrel with a few of each or even one of each); the rest of them seem to be decks that are !Gangrel by virtue of having 5 or 6 !Gangrel, of which 4 or 5 are the same minion (Enkidu, Aksinya, Una; Sebastian Goulet and his Advanced version show up as a superstar in 3 or 4 decks). Many of the !Gangrel decks in the TWDA are 4 of a given !Gangrel superstar (Enkidu or Aksinya, generally) and then exactly 1 more completely exchangeable weenie !Gangrel (Denette?), presumably to get to 5 of the !Gangrel in the crypt to count as an !Gangrel deck for TWDA purposes (at least 5 of one clan, no more minions of another clan I think are the requirements).

This isn't, like, a condemnation of anything, just seeing that, in fact, most of the TWDA !Gangrel decks are really only effectively !Gangrel decks by virtue of technicality, rather than !Gangrel decks in spirit.

Actions to get votes can be pretty strong, votes to get votes on the other hand, it really depends on the situation.

Consider: I try to Crusade: Rome
1 stealth undirected action, one vote automatically for it. Title goes on the *acting vampire*.
Say someone has intercept or a vote card (or the edge, or a title), now you need stealth and/or vote push (unless someone will help you).

Now consider Bloodbath
1 stealth action requiring an archbishop, priscus, cardinal or regent to give one vote to a 5+ capacity vampire. Can be blocked, but no issue of voting applies.

Ignoring the blood part, which is sort of interesting, I have thrown a copy of Bloodbath in my g2/3 Tzim toolbox deck because I wanted to have more permanent votes and the crypt already supported it. If I wanted to play a crusade card casually, I would usually have to be winning in votes already, so what's the point?

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
> Ashur wrote:
> In 16 years, I have never seen anyone play Bloodbath or Blood Siege. Not even in casual games, not even in limited games. I think I know why they are underplayed
>
They're really not that bad at all.

Bloodbath can essentially give you votes without needing to pass political actions. Really good if you have cheap Archbishops or Prisci (Fabrizia obviously, Shawnda, 7-caps). Works well with the !Toreador (with Foundation Exhibit, each guy with a Bloodbath has the same votes as a Prince/Archbishop) or the !Tremere (with Orlando Oriundus). If the Pander actually had bigger vampires, it would be really good with Legacy of Pander. For something a bit trickier, you could play Bloodbath on 5-caps before going Anarch (which then stack with Firebrands and provide a backup in case your Fee Stakes get voted out).

The greatest strength of Blood Siege is removing the Prince title (getting an Archbishop is just gravy). Not being able to play action mods makes it hard to use, but the !Ventrue can still use it best with Demonstration, along with Quentin or Bruce or Laszlo. Also not that bad with Orlando Oriundus (each blood is worth 2) or Terrifisto (people are unlikely to burn too much blood since they might take damage). Dia de los Muertos or Powerbase: Madrid also help. Or you can just use this as the vote after Cryptic Rider / Charming Lobby. Heh, Blood Siege decks might be one of the few situations where Distant Friend actually becomes a useful choice. Could also be hilarious if you follow up a failed Blood Siege (because someone burned lots of blood) with a Tribunal Judgment!

With all the concern about Prince/Justicar decks, I'm surprised people haven't tried building anti-P/J decks with the Ventrue Antitribu. Framing an Ancient Grudge eliminates Princes and Primogen (and Justicars if you pay the pool). Fear of Mekhet deals with IC's. Gustav Mallenhous neutralizes any Bishops or Archbishops around. Demonstration, Quentin, and Kindred Manipulation take care of any voters left. Slotting in a Blood Siege or two (for added Prince removal, on top of Framing) is just gravy. If you have the space, you could even include a copy of Rastacourere.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body:
I have played all three clans quite a bit, and I have to say that !Gangrel is definetily the worst. I have a semi ok !Gangrel mono protean rush deck with lot of agg damage, amaranths, and gangrel conspiracies which sometimes wins games, but dies if it faces lot of prevent or s:ce. I also had quite a bit of success with Sebastian Goulet satyr deck, but that wasn't really !gangrel deck so much, as it used dom/obf/pro. Although crypt was mainly !gangrel (basic and advanced Goulet and Philippe,) with just couple DOM/obf support vampires off-clan).

!Nos I have made several quite well working decks with, best was probably group 2-3 midcap toolbox with some black hand tech (Teresita with watchtower four ride forth, and some corporal reservoirs and truth in inks), they can also make fairly decent stealth vote decks with group 3-4, as they have nice grooming chain of titled vampires, but that still never worked as well to me as similar concept with !malks who had the advantage of The Call and bounce.

!Brujah is the best of those three clans by far, they can do good vote decks, good rush decks, good bleed decks, about only thing they can't do is intercept. They also have lot of out of clan obfuscate in group 3-4 if you want to go that way. They have great midcaps in group 2-3, and great big caps in 3-4. About only problem I can think of for !Brujah is that their clan cards (apart from Gang Territory) are fairly weak.
